problem: Retain large-VLM semantic conditioning while producing robot actions fast enough for changing scenes.
contribution: HiRT separates a slower asynchronously refreshed VLM latent from a lightweight policy processing fresh image context.
algorithm: InstructBLIP/Q-Former/LLM features are pooled into a cached latent. Condition the faster visual/action policy via FiLM, cross-attention and MAP prefix tokens. Train with randomly delayed visual context to tolerate stale latents, LoRA VLM adaptation and continuous-regression/discrete-status losses.
observations: Wrist/third-person image histories, task instruction and a possibly stale semantic latent. Fast observation updates are distinct from the slower language-model update rate.
actions: Relative end-effector or continuous joint actions plus discrete end-effector status; target control representation must be specified for each robot.
embodiment_and_data: MetaWorld20tasks×50demos, Franka-Kitchen5tasks×100demos and2000physical Franka trajectories across4skills.
experiments: Simulation20attempts/task in MetaWorld and100in Kitchen; real tasks20attempts each. Dynamic targets move roughly1cm/s, with seen/unseen objects and distractors; ablations remove image context or conditioning.
baselines: Diffusion Policy, RT-1 and a local Vanilla-VLA reimplementation of RT-2. The local reimplementation is not the original web-scale RT-2 checkpoint.

quantitative_result.value: Dynamic table reports HiRT75%average versusVanilla-VLA48%; inference benchmark9.8Hz versus4.1Hz. Table2 time6.18s is explicitly measured on corresponding quasi-static scenes, not moving-object completion duration. Static real average70.0% trailsVanilla-VLA71.3%.
quantitative_result.location: PDF p6 Table1/setup, p7 Table2 and explanation

limitations: Cached semantic latents can be stale despite training augmentation; tests do not include fast-flying targets or rapid posture adjustment. Faster inference does not uniformly improve static performance or prove safe reaction times.
code_and_license: Primary architecture and protocols examined; exact source revision, model rights and execution were not audited. No local HiRT reproduction is claimed.
hardware_adaptation: Relevant dual-rate architecture reference, requiring explicit semantic-latent age, fresh images and controller timing. Benchmark end-to-end NX latency and stop behavior rather than substituting source processing Hz for physical control bandwidth.
